newsitem.title: NORWAY: Greenspan makes small Norway shareholders nervous.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan makes small Norway shareholders nervous.

text.p: Small Norwegian shareholders sold stock but institutional investors stayed calm on Thursday following a warning from U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on share valuations, brokers said.
The Total index closed 0.84 percent lower at 1,078.43 points. Turnover was moderate at 810 million crowns.
"Small shareholders got nervous after Greenspan's speech," one broker said. "But institutional investors are sitting on their positions. I think the market will go up again."
Another broker said: "If the United States is stable next week the market will correct itself upwards."

Another reason for the fall was an advice from Norway's Banking, Insurance and Securities Commission to banks and insurance companies they had to cut costs to stay reasonably profitable. Both the banking and insurance indexes slipped.
Industrial giant Norsk Hydro rose 2.50 crowns to 337.50 crowns after losing ground since releasing disappointing 1996 profits on Monday.
Kvaerner's A share was up two crowns at 337 crowns after NatWest Securities said it was upgrading the industrial group to buy from hold.
